newTokensProposed.name: --shadow-base
newTokensProposed.why: The ink of every ad-hoc drop shadow. --shadow is a whole box-shadow value and so cannot be reused at the 11 sites with their own geometry, and this patch swaps colour literals, not declarations. Paired with --shadow-strength in a color-mix it themes the hue while dark stays byte-identical (#000 at the original alpha). Light value is the same 23,20,15 ink --shadow's paper value already uses.

newTokensProposed.name: --shadow-strength
newTokensProposed.why: Alpha multiplier so one color-mix expression serves both modes: color-mix(in srgb, var(--shadow-base) calc(A% * var(--shadow-strength)), transparent). Dark leaves A untouched, so every replacement is a no-op. 0.31 is derived, not invented — it is the exact ratio --shadow already applies (.45 -> .14), so a .45 site reproduces --shadow's paper alpha of .14 and heavier sites scale in proportion. Avoids inventing a token per alpha (.45/.5/.55/.6/.62/.65 all appear).

newTokensProposed.name: --ink-wash-base
newTokensProposed.why: 22 of the 42 sites use rgba(245,240,232,a) — #f5f0e8, a warmer off-white than --text (#f5f4f0). Folding them onto var(--text) is a rounding: at the alphas in use (.045–.26) it moves G/B by up to 2/255 in dark mode, so it violates the byte-identical rule. This token carries the exact dark value and inverts to the same #17140f ink as --text on paper. It exists only to hold the drift; see needsHumanDecision — the team may prefer to retire #f5f0e8 into --text the way the three reading greys were retired into --text-body, which would delete this token.

newTokensProposed.name: --veil-base
newTokensProposed.why: The themed counterpart to --scrim. Half the warm near-black rgba(12,10,9,α) sites are NOT chrome — song and car hero scrims, in-card failure overlays, photo badges, the map popover — and every one of them contains text that flips to ink, so their ground must flip to paper. --bg cannot serve them: --bg's dark value is #0a0a0b, so color-mix(var(--bg) 82%) would change the dark render. Dark #0c0a09 is byte-identical to today's base; light is the paper ground, so color-mix(in srgb, var(--veil-base) N%, transparent) darkens a photo in dark mode and lightens it on paper with one expression. (--bg already plays this role, byte-identically, for the 24 cool rgba(10,10,11,α) photo-scrim sites — no token needed there.)

newTokensProposed.name: --scrim-cool
newTokensProposed.why: Four chrome bars use the COOL near-black instead of --scrim's warm one, at two alphas: mobileAfrobeatsHub .backBar at .94, and mobileMusic / mobileRecords / mobileLiveCharts .backBar at .95, plus the nav-sheet dimmer at .72. Rule 4 says they stay dark, so they cannot be color-mix(var(--bg) …) — that would turn four mastheads and the sheet dimmer to paper. Fixed in both modes, it keeps dark byte-identical. Its dark value equals --bg's dark value, which is exactly why the naive fix is wrong and the token is worth having.

newTokensProposed.name: --scrim-deep
newTokensProposed.why: A fourth near-black base, rgba(8,7,6,α), used only by the two modal dimmers (statCardButton .backdrop at .5, music .backdrop at .6). A modal dimmer stays dark on paper, so it needs a fixed token; no existing one is byte-identical (#080706 vs --scrim's #0c0a09).

newTokensProposed.name: --photo-well
newTokensProposed.why: The opaque matte behind a car photograph (cars.module.css .tileImg and its mobile twin), visible only before the image paints. A fifth near-black that matches nothing in the table. Light value proposed as the --bg-raised paper so a loading tile does not flash a black rectangle in light mode — that light value is the open question, dark is byte-identical either way.

newTokensProposed.name: --scrim-base
newTokensProposed.why: The un-alpha'd warm scrim ink, FIXED in both modes, for the two map country-border strokes. They are dark-on-light hairlines even in dark mode (near-black on --bg-soft-2), so they must stay dark on paper too — the themed --veil-base would erase them. Also available as the fixed base for any future chrome scrim at an alpha other than .94.

needsHumanDecision.question: Ten sites paint text on a gold fill with #0a0a0b, but the table's token for that role is --ink-on-gold = #14100a. Using the right token changes dark by 4/0/1 in RGB (invisible on a gold chip) and so breaks the strict dark-is-a-no-op rule. Do you bless --ink-on-gold as a fourth blessed consolidation for these ten, or do you want a byte-identical --ink-on-gold-cool (#0a0a0b) kept alongside it? Recommendation: bless the consolidation — two near-black inks on the same gold ramp is the drift the split is meant to end. Affects artist.module.css:493, certifications.module.css:785, StatCardMaker:76 and :141, mobileAfricasBiggest:219, mobileCerts:243, mobileOfficialCharts:380, mobileTourMap:181, mobileTours:163 and :276.

The three .actionPrimary rules (mobileOfficialCharts:376-380, mobileTourMap:177-181, mobileTours:272-276) each declare colour on the gold ramp three times: color:#000, -webkit-text-fill-color:#000, then color:#0a0a0b. WebKit paints #000 and ignores the later declaration, so Safari and Firefox already disagree. Should all three collapse to a single color: var(--ink-on-gold) with the -webkit-text-fill-color line deleted? The #000 pair sits in the pure-black family, not the scrim family, so it needs to be patched in step with these or light mode will theme one browser and not the other.

Four chrome bars use the cool near-black (mobileAfrobeatsHub .backBar at rgba(10,10,11,.94); mobileMusic, mobileRecords, mobileLiveCharts .backBar at .95) where every other bar on the site uses --scrim's rgba(12,10,9,.94). Do you want the new --scrim-cool token to preserve them byte-for-byte, or should they simply be normalised onto var(--scrim)? The visible change would be about one RGB step and would delete a token and a long-standing inconsistency. Recommendation: normalise onto --scrim, if you accept the sub-perceptual dark-mode change.

The two modal dimmers use rgba(8,7,6,α), a base found nowhere else. Keep --scrim-deep to hold dark byte-identical, or fold them onto var(--scrim-base) at the same alphas (a 4/3/3 RGB shift, invisible at 50-60% opacity over content)? Folding would cut the family from five new tokens to four.

The tour map's country borders are a near-black hairline at 90% over pale-ish shapes. Holding dark byte-identical means light mode gets that same near-black border, which will read considerably heavier against the paper base map than it does today against --bg-soft-2. Do you want a themed stroke instead (light-dark(rgba(23,20,15,.30), rgba(12,10,9,.9)), i.e. --rule-soft's light value with today's dark preserved)? That keeps dark identical and lightens only the paper map. It needs a new token, so it is your call whether the map warrants one.

The car-photo matte (#0a0908, also at mobileDeepPage:372) shows only while the image loads or if it letterboxes. Should it go pale in light mode as proposed (--photo-well light #e6e0d4), or stay dark so the photo always sits in a black well in both themes? Dark is byte-identical either way; this is purely how a loading tile should look on paper.

problems.problem: SYSTEMIC DARK DRIFT, 46 of 109 sites. I read app/globals.css myself: --text-body is declared once at line 53 as light-dark(#4a443b, #cfc7bb), so its DARK value is #cfc7bb. That makes the 63 #cfc7bb decisions genuine byte-identical no-ops (verified line by line; the classifier's darkIdentical:true is correct on all 63). But the 37 #d8d8de and 9 #d3d3da decisions all carry darkIdentical:false and every one of them CHANGES dark. #d8d8de -> #cfc7bb drops contrast on --bg (#0a0a0b) from 13.94:1 to 12.16:1; #d3d3da -> #cfc7bb drops it from 13.13:1 to 12.16:1. Luminance is the smaller half of it: #d8d8de and #d3d3da are cool blue-greys (B > R = G) and #cfc7bb is a warm beige (R > G > B), so this is a visible hue rotation across 46 sites in dark mode, not a rounding. Per HARD RULE 1 this is the blessed three-grey consolidation and the classifier does flag it explicitly at every one of the 46 sites (I checked each note individually — none is silently merged), so it is admissible. I am recording it so the drift is signed off with its real magnitude rather than waved through on the 'darkIdentical' column. The eight most visible instances are data cells that sit beside cool var(--text-muted) #9b9ba3 siblings in the same table row, where the warm shift reads as a temperature mismatch rather than a tone change: records.module.css:204 (.tour) and :209 (.tickets), tours.module.css:206 (.dCity), :212 (.dCap), :273 (.tourCell), :278 (.tickets), revenue.module.css:133 (.tour), mobileHome.module.css:422 (.boardName). Coverage itself is complete and correct: grep finds exactly 63 + 37 + 9 = 109 in-scope occurrences, matching globals.css:51-52's own tally, and the 64th #cfc7bb (app/lib/statCardImage.tsx:280) is rightly excluded as a permanently-dark ImageResponse render.
problems.claimed: 46 sites: #d8d8de / #d3d3da -> var(--text-body), 'dark shifts to #cfc7bb by design'
problems.correction: Accept as the table's blessed consolidation, but record it as a real dark-mode change, not a no-op: 46 sites move from a cool grey to a warm beige, ~13% contrast loss (13.94:1 -> 12.16:1). If dark must be a strict pixel no-op for this migration, the 37 #d8d8de and 9 #d3d3da sites need their own tokens (--text-body-cool at light-dark(#4a443b, #d8d8de)) instead; otherwise sign off explicitly on the 46-site warming.

problems.problem: BREAKS DARK AT ALL 13 COLOR-MIX SITES. The new token --shadow-strength is a unitless NUMBER, and the proposal gives it a dark and a light value without saying how it is declared. globals.css:249-252 carries its own warning on exactly this point ("light-dark() takes COLOURS") and is why --shadow and --glow already live in the :root[data-theme="light"] override block. An implementer following the file's dominant convention writes `--shadow-strength: light-dark(1, 0.31)`, which is not a valid <color> and not a valid <number>. Custom properties parse anything, so the failure surfaces at substitution: `calc(55% * light-dark(1, 0.31))` is invalid, the color-mix is invalid, and the whole box-shadow declaration becomes invalid-at-computed-value-time -> `unset` -> box-shadow: none. Dark mode loses the shadow entirely at all 13 sites, silently, with no CSS error. This is a spec gap in the new token, not a hypothetical: nothing in the proposal rules the wrong form out.

TOKEN VALUES CONFIRMED (read from globals.css, not trusted from the table): --text light-dark(#17140f, #f5f4f0); --line dark rgba(245,244,240,.12); --rule dark rgba(245,244,240,.38); --rule-soft dark rgba(245,244,240,.24); --bg dark #0a0a0b; --bg-soft dark #141416; --bg-soft-2 dark #1c1c21; --bg-raised dark #24242a; --gold: var(--gold-ink) = #ffb627 dark; --scrim rgba(12,10,9,.94) (no light-dark, does not theme).

THE 42 REPLACEMENTS THEMSELVES ARE DARK NO-OPS. color-mix(in srgb, C p%, transparent) mixes premultiplied in a rectangular space, so it yields exactly rgba(C, p/100) — the idiom globals.css already ships at --color-accent-100 and .tagAccent. Both proposed new tokens carry the correct dark bytes (#f5f0e8, #ffffff). I found no drift in any replacement as written.

BOTH NEW TOKENS ARE JUSTIFIED, and I verified the drift they exist to hold rather than trusting the claim: #f5f0e8 vs #f5f4f0 at a=.045 over #0a0a0b rounds G to 20 vs 21; at a=.26 it rounds B to 68 vs 71. #ffffff vs #f5f4f0 at a=.015 over #0a0a0b rounds B to 15 vs 14. Neither can be folded onto --text.

WHAT I FOUND instead lives in the notes: two of them recommend follow-up consolidations whose arithmetic is wrong and which WOULD break dark; three misdescribe the compositing or scoping at the call site in ways that would send a reviewer to the wrong conclusion; and the family has a scope gap into .tsx.

OPERATIONAL WARNING: app/globals.css was being rewritten by a concurrent process during this review. Its md5 changed twice (0f418a41 -> e7540f0b) and --line moved from line 18 to line 25. The token VALUES were stable across all reads, but any patch must locate declarations by content, not by line number, and re-read globals.css immediately before editing.

problems.problem: The note recommends deleting --white-wash-base and folding these three sites onto var(--text), on the arithmetic "at 1.5% the delta is under 1/255". That arithmetic is wrong at the rendered pixel. #ffffff at a=.015 over --bg #0a0a0b gives B = .015*255 + .985*11 = 14.66 -> 15; var(--text) #f5f4f0 at the same alpha gives B = .015*240 + .985*11 = 14.44 -> 14. One byte of drift, in dark, at the SMALLEST alpha in the set. Over --bg-soft #141416 the red channel splits too (23.53 -> 24 vs 23.38 -> 23), and the other two sites (.02, .04) drift further. The same false claim is repeated in the --white-wash-base token rationale ("the cheapest fix may be to normalise the file onto --text instead of shipping this token").

problems.problem: The note says this and app/analysis/analysis.module.css:194 are "same job and same alpha, but that one is #f5f0e8-based, so the two get different bases despite one design intent - worth normalising later." Normalising either onto the other's base breaks dark. At a=.26 over #0a0a0b: #f5f0e8 gives B = .26*232 + .74*11 = 68.46 -> 68; #f5f4f0 gives B = .26*240 + .74*11 = 70.54 -> 71. Three bytes of drift in blue, one in green. Separately, the --ink-wash-base rationale understates exactly this: it says the drift is "up to 2/255" across the .045-.26 range, when the true maximum is 3/255 in blue at .26. The understatement happens to argue for the token, so the conclusion survives, but the number is wrong and it is the number a reviewer would use to decide whether the token is worth keeping.

problems.problem: The note computes this wash over the wrong backdrop, and the wrong backdrop is what licensed the whole decision. The wash therefore composites over the --rule seam bed, not over #0a0a0b. Actual dark result: --rule rgba(245,244,240,.38) over #0a0a0b ~ rgb(99,99,98), then 5.5% #f5f0e8 over that ~ #6b6b69 - a mid grey, not #191817. This is precisely the failure the DaiDaiConquest.module.css file header documents ("a bare translucent background against that mid-grey read as olive/washed-out"), and it is why app/api/api.module.css:96 and DaiDaiConquest:28 use the linear-gradient-over-var(--bg) device that this rule does not. The proposed color-mix is still a dark no-op, so nothing regresses - but on paper the seam bed becomes --rule light rgba(23,20,15,.48) over #f7f4ee ~ rgb(139,137,133), and a hovered TOC card lands around #84837f: a dark grey slab on white, not a lift.

problems.problem: The note's WARNING is factually wrong against the current globals.css and raises a needsHumanDecision for a non-problem. problems.problem: RULE 3 IN REVERSE, ~30 sites — the largest defect in this family. The mapping says "CHROME, stays dark" and stops. But every one of these bars is a CSS-module class, NOT .navbar, so its CONTENTS keep resolving light-dark() against the page's light scheme while the bar itself stays near-black. .tab is `color: var(--text-muted)` → light #5f584f on a #1a1817-composited bar = 2.61:1 at 11px (today 6.63:1). .tabOn is `color: var(--gold)` → #8a5a00 = 3.26:1 — the ACTIVE tab. Worse on the back bars: .backLabel inherits `color: var(--text)` → #17140f on near-black = 1.02:1, i.e. the page title in every mobile back bar is literally invisible in light mode. And `border-bottom/top: 1px solid var(--line)` flips to rgba(23,20,15,.12) — a black hairline on a black bar, so all ~30 bars silently lose their divider. Rule 3 says to flag "any site where the background themes but its text does not (or vice versa)"; this is the vice-versa case and the mapping flags none of it.

problems.claimed: var(--ink-on-gold) — "In WebKit the text-fill-color wins… Safari and Firefox will theme differently"
problems.correction: The browser claim is backwards. -webkit-text-fill-color has been implemented in Gecko since Firefox 49 and is honoured by every current engine, so #000 at line 377 paints EVERYWHERE and `color: #0a0a0b` at line 380 never paints in any browser. Consequence: this replacement is a pure no-op — it changes no pixel in either theme. Record it as such, and record that the only decision that actually matters here belongs to the pure-black family (line 377). `color` at 380 still feeds currentColor and inheritance, so map it for consistency, but do not claim it fixes the label. Identical at mobileTourMap.module.css:181 (fill at 178) and mobileTours.module.css:276 (fill at 273).

problems.claimed: color-mix(in srgb, var(--veil-base) 97%, transparent), role "wash"

As specified, --veil-base is asked to serve five distinct roles across its 11 sites — full-cover overlay (StatCardMaker:109, mobileStatCards:236, statCardButton:107), photo chip (mobileDeepPage:384, cars:290), inset panel (car.module.css:97), hero scrim (song.module.css:76 ×3) and floating popover (this line). One token, five roles, is the same collapse the gold split exists to prevent.

problems.claimed: Five new fixed/near-black tokens (--veil-base, --scrim-cool, --scrim-deep, --scrim-base, --photo-well) minted so dark stays byte-identical, while eight --ink-on-gold sites accept a dark shift
problems.correction: Apply one standard. --veil-base dark #0c0a09 vs --bg dark #0a0a0b differs by (2,0,2)/255 and its light value #f7f4ee is byte-identical to --bg's; --scrim-cool is #0a0a0b, byte-identical to --bg's dark; --photo-well dark #0a0908 differs from --bg by (0,1,3)/255 and its light value #e6e0d4 is byte-identical to --bg-raised's. Meanwhile #0a0a0b → --ink-on-gold #14100a is a (10,6,1)/255 shift accepted with a shrug. Either hold rule 1 strictly everywhere (and mint an --ink-on-gold-deep for the eight chip labels) or relax it consistently and collapse --veil-base/--scrim-cool/--photo-well onto --bg / --scrim / --bg-raised. Five single-purpose near-blacks whose roles are already named in the table is over-tokenization; the roles here are page-ground-at-alpha, chrome backdrop, and image matte, all of which exist.
problems.problem: Internally inconsistent application of hard rule 1: strict byte-identity is enforced for backgrounds nobody can distinguish, and waived for text where the delta is 2.5× larger. The result is a token set where role, not colour, has stopped deciding the name.

problems.claimed: color-mix(in srgb, var(--scrim-base) 90%, transparent), fixed in both modes, role "data"
problems.correction: Keeping it fixed is the right call for dark-identity, but state the light-mode consequence numerically and put it to the designer: 0.9-alpha near-black on #efeae1 gives a near-3:1-plus hairline grid, while every other structural line on the site is --rule at rgba(23,20,15,0.48). Propose --scrim-base as light-dark(rgba-equivalent of --rule at the map's weight, #0c0a09) or accept the divergence explicitly. Line 217 must move with it.
problems.problem: The role is 'structural line separating two data regions' — which is exactly what --rule is defined as (globals.css:32, 3.30:1, clears WCAG 3:1). Pinning it to a fixed 0.9 near-black gives the tour map a border weight roughly twice every other structural rule on the paper theme. Role-correct, weight-inconsistent.

problems.claimed: color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 55%, transparent) — "Its text is var(--muted)… so the chip ground must theme with them"
problems.correction: Measure before asserting. --muted aliases --text-muted (globals.css:200), light #5f584f. On paper-at-55% over the grayscale(0.35) press shot the composite ground is ≈ rgb(185,183,180), giving 3.47:1 at 11px bold uppercase — below AA, and below today's dark measurement of 4.31:1 (itself already marginal). problems.problem: Same unmeasured 'themes with it' reasoning as the .anchorTag sites: a 55% wash is not a surface, and the ink that lands on it in light mode is a mid grey, not the near-white the dark render relies on.

problems.claimed: --scrim-cool, "sites: 4"
